title: Feature Selection Quiz
description: Test your understanding of feature selection techniques and best practices

questions.text: What is the primary goal of feature selection?
options: To increase the number of features in the dataset
To select a subset of relevant features that improve model performance
To convert categorical features to numerical features
To normalize all features to the same scale
questions.explanation: Feature selection aims to identify and select the most relevant features from the original feature set, which can improve model performance, reduce overfitting, and decrease computational cost.

questions.text: Which type of feature selection method evaluates features independently of the learning algorithm?
questions.explanation: Filter methods evaluate features independently of the learning algorithm using statistical measures like correlation, mutual information, or variance. They are fast but may miss feature interactions.

questions.text: Wrapper methods are more computationally expensive than filter methods because they use the learning algorithm to evaluate features.
questions.explanation: True. Wrapper methods use the actual learning algorithm to evaluate different feature subsets, requiring multiple model training iterations, which makes them more computationally expensive than filter methods.

questions.text: Which feature selection method is best for capturing non-linear relationships between features and target?
questions.explanation: Mutual information can capture both linear and non-linear relationships between features and target variables, making it more versatile than correlation-based methods that only capture linear relationships.

questions.text: When should feature selection be applied in the machine learning pipeline?
options: Before splitting the data into train and test sets
After splitting, using only the training data to select features
It doesn't matter when you apply it
questions.explanation: Feature selection should be applied after data splitting, using only the training data to select features. This prevents data leakage from the test set and ensures unbiased evaluation of model performance.

A wrapper method that iteratively removes the least important features
An embedded method that uses L1 regularization
A method that only works with categorical features
questions.explanation: RFE is a wrapper method that recursively trains models and eliminates the least important features until a desired number of features is reached. It considers feature interactions but is computationally expensive.

questions.text: Which regularization technique naturally performs feature selection by driving feature weights to zero?
questions.explanation: L1 regularization (Lasso) adds a penalty proportional to the absolute value of coefficients, which can drive some coefficients to exactly zero, effectively performing automatic feature selection.

questions.text: What is a major risk when applying feature selection too aggressively on small datasets?
questions.explanation: Aggressive feature selection on small datasets can lead to overfitting, where the selected features work well on the training data but don't generalize to new data. This is especially problematic when the number of features approaches the number of samples.

questions.text: Which feature selection approach combines the benefits of filter and wrapper methods?
questions.explanation: Embedded methods perform feature selection as part of the model training process, combining the efficiency of filter methods with the algorithm-awareness of wrapper methods. Examples include L1 regularization and tree-based feature importance.

questions.text: Why might correlation-based feature selection miss important features?
options: It always selects too many features
questions.explanation: Correlation-based feature selection only captures linear relationships between features and the target. It may miss features that have important non-linear relationships or features that are only useful in combination with other features.
